📌 Governance Snapshots: Why Your Tokens May Not Count in a DAO Vote

Main Points
⏺ Some DAOs calculate voting power using token balances from a specific blockchain block
⏺ Buying tokens after that snapshot may not increase your voting power
⏺ This post explains how balance snapshots work and why purchase timing matters

1️⃣ Core Idea — the protocol records balances at a selected block to determine how many votes each participant receives.
2️⃣ Why It Exists — a fixed reference point prevents voting power from changing every time tokens are transferred during the voting process.
3️⃣ Example — a vote uses balances from block #1000, but you buy tokens at block #1005. Those new tokens won't increase your voting power for that proposal.
4️⃣ Risk Surface — users may buy governance tokens specifically to participate, only to discover the snapshot already happened.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — before buying governance tokens, check the snapshot block, delegation conditions, and voting eligibility rules.

Final Thoughts

DAO governance isn't only about how many tokens you hold. It can also depend on when you held them. Sometimes your voting power is decided before the vote even begins.

THE BOOMERANG EFFECT: ISRAEL'S LEFT FACES ITS OWN CAMPAIGN ARGUMENTS

There is a striking political irony unfolding in Israel following the elections. Two of the opposition's biggest campaign issues are now colliding with the realities of coalition negotiations. And the left-leaning media outlets that amplified those campaign messages face the same questions about consistency.

FIRST—THE HAREDI DRAFT.

For months, opposition politicians, backed by sympathetic media coverage, presented ultra-Orthodox military conscription as an urgent national security issue, essential to the IDF, national equality, and Israel's very survival.

Now comes the real test. With the opposition falling short of the seats needed to form a government, will those same politicians suddenly discover room for negotiations, compromises, and exemptions if bringing Haredi parties into a coalition becomes politically convenient?

And will the same media commentators who treated every proposed compromise as a national emergency now defend flexibility when it serves a different coalition?

What was portrayed as a national emergency before the elections cannot simply become a negotiable political bargaining chip afterward without serious questions being asked.

SECOND—QATAR.

Throughout the campaign, Netanyahu faced fierce accusations over the Qatar affair, including allegations of betrayal. Opposition politicians and critical media outlets devoted extensive attention to those accusations.

Now, with neither bloc holding a majority, the opposition faces difficult questions about potential cooperation with Arab parties amid an investigation into suspected foreign funding, reportedly involving Qatar, intended to influence the election.

Those allegations remain under investigation and do not establish wrongdoing by the Arab parties themselves. But the question of political consistency remains: Will the same politicians and media outlets demand equally rigorous scrutiny regardless of which political camp is affected?

THE REAL TEST OF POLITICAL PRINCIPLES IS WHETHER THEY SURVIVE THE PURSUIT OF POWER.

If military conscription was essential to Israel's survival yesterday, it should remain essential today. If alleged Qatari interference demanded scrutiny when Netanyahu was the target, the same standards should apply to everyone.

And if the media presented these issues as matters of national principle during the campaign, it should hold every potential coalition to those same standards afterward.

POLITICAL PRINCIPLES SHOULD NOT CHANGE WITH COALITION ARITHMETIC—AND NEITHER SHOULD JOURNALISTIC STANDARDS.

👀 Justin Sun becomes PEPE’s largest individual holder, Arkham says 

🌐 Tron founder Justin Sun has accumulated nearly 3% of PEPE’s supply, with blockchain analytics firm Arkham Intelligence identifying approximately $51.25 million worth of the memecoin across his known and suspected wallets. According to an October 27 Arkham Intelligence report, the tokens entered Sun-linked wallets over the previous 10 days, making him the largest individual PEPE holder outside cryptocurrency exchanges.

🔗 The firm estimated his combined holdings at 2.82% of PEPE’s supply, although some wallets included in its calculations were attributed to Sun through blockchain analysis. At the time, PEPE had a market capitalization of approximately $1.81 billion, with exchanges controlling several of the largest known holdings.

📊 Binance held $337.5 million worth of PEPE, representing 18.7% of the supply, followed by Robinhood with $150.9 million, or 8.37%. Coinbase and OKX accounted for another 5.03% and 4.15%, respectively. Unlike Sun’s attributed holdings, exchange balances generally include assets held on behalf of customers, meaning their large positions do not necessarily represent investments made by the platforms themselves.
